hook: He spent 27 years in prison, then led South Africa from apartheid to democracy.

pages.x: Nelson Mandela was born in 1918 in Mvezo, a village in South Africa. His first name, Rolihlahla, means "pulling the branch of a tree", or troublemaker. A teacher gave him the name Nelson.

In Johannesburg he became a lawyer and joined the African National Congress. In 1952 he and Oliver Tambo opened the first Black law firm in the country, while the white government built apartheid, a system of strict racial separation.
After police shot dead 69 protesters at Sharpeville in 1960, and the ANC was banned, he helped set up its armed wing, which sabotaged government targets. He was arrested in 1962.

At his trial in 1964 he spoke for three hours from the dock, ending with his hope of a free country where all lived together as equals: an ideal, he said, he was prepared to die for. He was sentenced to life in prison.
For 18 of his 27 years in prison he was held on Robben Island, breaking rocks in a lime quarry whose glare damaged his eyes. He studied law by post, and secretly wrote his memoirs.
Campaigns all over the world demanded his release. On 11 February 1990, aged 71, he walked out of prison, his fist raised.
He negotiated the end of apartheid with President de Klerk, and they shared the Nobel Peace Prize. In 1994, in the first election open to all races, he became South Africa's first Black president.
In 1995 he walked onto the field wearing the jersey of the Springboks, the national rugby team, long a symbol of white South Africa, when they won the World Cup. White fans chanted his name.
He set up a Truth and Reconciliation Commission to face the crimes of apartheid, and stepped down after one term, in 1999. He died in 2013, aged 95.
Mandela ended apartheid through forgiveness rather than revenge, and became one of the most admired people in the world. His birthday, 18 July, is Nelson Mandela Day.
pts: Spent 27 years in prison fighting apartheid
